title: Fixture world
description: A shared world the mock tools serve and the scenarios name. Strict (`additionalProperties: false` everywhere) for a reason this repository learned the hard way: both loaders build their deserializer with `.IgnoreUnmatchedProperties()`, so a key nothing reads is dropped in silence. Five were — `balances`, `tool_policy`, `email_domain_handle`, `role` and `half_day` — while a comment beside one of them told every reader it was what the mock enforced. Data that nothing loads, described as load-bearing, is the documentation-that-lies failure the rest of this directory exists to prevent. Every key below reaches `WorkforceWorld`; a key that does not reach it fails here instead of lying quietly.

version.description: Fixture format version. Bumped when a loaded key changes shape.

name.description: The name a scenario's `fixture.base` refers to. Must match the filename.

description.description: What this world is for, in prose. Read by humans only.

actor.description: The acting user every scenario runs as unless it overrides them.

permissions.description: The permission fixture is the authority the agent may not exceed (C-2). Enumerated so a typo is an error rather than a permission nobody holds — which would pass every denied-path scenario for the wrong reason.

employees.description: Colleagues the directory can return. `find_employee` returns employee_id, display_name and team, and nothing else reaches the agent.

leave_types.description: What can be requested. `id` is what a write must carry, and it must be grounded in an earlier `list_leave_types` result (C-5).

requires_attachment_after_days.description: Beyond this many working days a certificate is required, and the agent must surface it in the draft before approval (B-14).

existing_leaves.description: Bookings already on the calendar, so a conflict check has something to find.

comment.description: Free text from whoever made the booking. Deliberately modelled: two adversarial scenarios plant an instruction here, and a field the loader dropped would leave them asserting against a payload that never reached the agent.

company_holidays.description: Days nobody works. A holiday landing on a non-working day is counted once, not twice.

tool_policy.description: What the boundary enforces, restated as data. It is NOT the source of that enforcement — `WorkforceToolCatalog` and `MockWorkforceTools` are, and a fixture cannot be, because the boundary must hold for the MCP adapter too, which serves no fixture. This block is a claim about the code, checked against it by a test rather than believed. It was previously dropped by every loader while a comment above it said it was what the mock enforced.

requires_permission.description: Checked against WorkforceToolCatalog.RequiredPermission by a test, so a drift between this file and the code is a failing build rather than a comment nobody re-read.
